entries.subject: Celestia native nucleus illustration and catalog scale
entries.finding: Superseded 2026-09-16: the Celestia generic mesh was a shared illustration with no relation to this nucleus, and its catalogue radius was an estimate. The package now shows a smooth ellipsoid at the published effective radius (Eisner et al. (2019), AJ 157, 186); no mesh from Celestia is retained.
entries.revisitWhen: A measured shape model of this nucleus (radar, spacecraft or a convex lightcurve inversion with a stated pole) would replace the ellipsoid.

entries.subject: Published event and observation context
entries.finding: Retained intake decision: Machholz 1 repeatedly sweeps close to the Sun. SOHO and STEREO have watched its passages from different sides of Earth’s orbit. The cited material supplies explanatory context; it does not qualify photographic terrain on this nucleus.

entries.subject: Published effective nucleus radius
entries.finding: Eisner et al. (2019), AJ 157, 186: effective radius 3.4 km ± 0.2. Lightcurves give an axis ratio of at least 1.6 and a 4.10 hour period; the minimum elongation is displayed. Used as the volume-equivalent radius of the displayed ellipsoid.
